name: Harsini / Laki of Harsin
catalog_citation: Belelli, Sara. 2021. The Laki variety of Harsin: grammar, texts, lexicon (Bamberger Orientstudien). Bamberg: University of Bamberg Press. Open access (CC-BY 4.0), PDF via fis.uni-bamberg.de.
catalog_quote: In Harsini, the position of lexical stress is largely predictable. Each word has a primary stress ... Monomorphemic lexical words and proper names formed by more than one syllable are generally stressed on the last syllable: nizī́k ‘near’ bowá ‘father’ ... An exception is represented by a few disyllabic adverbs and function words that are normally stressed on the first syllable. ... Polymorphemic words have different stress patterns, depending on the morpheme added to the stem. The definite suffix -a/-ka ..., the plural marker -al ..., the comparative and superlative suffixes -tir/-tirīn ... attract primary stress. When multiple morphemes potentially carrying the stress attach to the same phonological word, the stress falls on the last available host: köwš-il-á ‘the shoes’ ... audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is confirmed verbatim in the open-access PDF we hold at the stated locator (sec. 2.6, pp. 69-70). The source is a 2021, 516-page fieldwork reference grammar with an explicit stress section, the only grammar Glottolog lists for laki1244 and the most recent description of any Laki variety; the 'morphological' coding (final default on monomorphemic words; a closed set of stress-attracting suffixes vs unstressed clitics; verbal prefixes ni-/bi-/na- with their own behaviour; listed lexical exceptions with initial stress) follows the text directly. The only caveat is languoid scope: Harsini is an SK/Laki transitional variety rather than Lorestan Laki proper, so Lazard 1992 (print-only) would be a useful cross-check for the languoid as a whole, but nothing seen suggests the classification would change.
